speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present, and did they start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your history of diabetes, alcohol use, and steroid use, have you noticed any specific pain in your right shoulder, neck, or arm, or any numbness in a specific pattern of your fingers? Also, have you experienced any recent fevers or night sweats?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The symptoms of dull, aching, and burning pain alongside weight loss are concerning for a neoplastic or infectious process rather than simple neuropathy. Given your history of anabolic steroid use and weight loss, have you noticed any visible muscle atrophy in the right shoulder or arm, or any difficulty lifting your arm overhead?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor)
